Plans have been submitted to turn a historic outbuilding beside a Grade I listed building into a five-bedroom home. Mick Hilless has applied to Huntingdonshire District Council to turn a barn and office building linked to Bodsey House into a home on Bodsey Toll Road, Ramsey. Bodsey House is Grade I listed, meaning it is of exceptional interest. The property was once a 13th-century hermitage belonging to Ramsey Abbey but has since been altered and turned into a family home. The plans would turn the barn and office building at the rear of the site into one five-bedroom home. The historic barn is curtilage listed, which means it is legally protected as it sits within the grounds of a listed building. Documents by Scroxton Architects say the barn and office building are dilapidated and no longer suitable for modern agricultural or commercial use. The plans would demolish the modern open-sided portal barn at the rear and replace it with a two-storey extension forming a five-bedroom home. The site is about 1.8km north-east of Ramsey and covers 0.2 hectares. rawItems.title: Motorcyclist injured after crash with van on busy Cambs road
rawItems.content: A motorcyclist has been injured in a crash with a van on a busy Cambridgeshire road. Police were called to Oilmills Road, Pondersbridge, near Ramsey and Whittlesey, at around 8pm on Monday September 28. A spokesperson for Cambridgeshire Constabulary said a motorcyclist suffered minor injuries after a collision with a van. No arrests were made.

rawItems.title: Cambs High Sheriff praises hospice charity for its ‘exceptional care’
rawItems.content: A hospice in Milton has been praised for its "exceptional care" by the High Sheriff of Cambridgeshire during a recent visit. Francis Burkitt DL, High Sheriff of Cambridgeshire, visited East Anglia’s Children’s Hospices (EACH) in Milton to present certificates of appreciation to long-serving staff and volunteers. He was joined by his wife Jo and Jonathan Jelley MBE JP during the visit, which included a tour of the care floor and meetings with children, families, and staff. Francis said: "I was delighted to be given the chance to celebrate and thank some of those who do so much to support EACH’s work. The High Sheriff of Cambridgeshire visited EACH’s hospice in Milton (Image: EACH) "EACH is widely known and highly regarded as one of the very best organisations in our county, doing so much for children and families across Cambridgeshire. "It’s the people who help deliver that exceptional care and support, and I can’t speak highly enough of the wonderful staff who work here." He also recognised the vital role of volunteers, adding: "Likewise, the amazing volunteers who selflessly give their time. "That’s why I was so thrilled to honour and recognise the contribution made by people like Mick and Graham here at Milton." High Sheriff’s Certificates of Appreciation were awarded to staff members Sandra Holmes, Helen Thrower and Sallyann Parkin, as well as volunteers Mick Housden and Graham Shipley.
